decisions.quote:
The original study found that a threat appeal about climate change can increase risk
perception and activism intentions and that a humor appeal can also increase activism intentions
with a large sample of young adults. Using the same stimuli, measures, and experimental design
with a similar sample, we fail to replicate these main effects. We do, however, replicate age as a
moderator of humor’s effect on perceived risk, such that the humor appeal only persuaded
emerging adults (ages 18-21.9).
decisions.location: Primary original-specific abstract/discussion comparison; raw source chars[1490,1986), lines28-33
decisions.reason: The replication tested three preregistered hypotheses from Skurka et al. (2018): main effects on climate activism intentions (H1), the main effect of the threat appeal on perceived risk (H2), and age moderation of the humor appeal (H3). The authors explicitly frame their results as failing to replicate the main effects (H1 and H2) while replicating age as a moderator of humor's effect on perceived risk (partially supporting H3, as well as finding null effects on personal mitigation behaviors consistent with the original study). Under the codebook rules, when tested findings partly replicate and partly fail to replicate as framed by the authors, the outcome is 'mixed'.
